name: Iowa

sales.rateNote: 6% state sales and use tax on tangible personal property, specified digital products and enumerated services; most jurisdictions add a 1% local option sales tax (LOST).

local.levies: local option sales tax (LOST) approved by voters in counties, cities or unincorporated areas of a county
local.capNote: LOST is 1% where authorized; it cannot apply to anything exempt from state sales tax, and there is no local option use tax.

groceries.note: Food and food ingredients are generally exempt (Iowa Code 423.3(57)); candy, soft drinks and prepared food are taxable. SNAP purchases are exempt.

clothing.note: Clothing is taxable except during the annual August holiday (articles under $100).

otherRates.note: Exempt from sales tax; instead a fee for new registration of $10 plus 5% of the sales or lease price, also on private-party sales.
State hotel and motel tax of 5% (not 6%), plus a local hotel/motel tax of up to 7%; local option sales tax does not apply.

otherRates.item: short-term car rentals (60 days or less)
otherRates.note: 5% automobile rental excise tax in addition to sales tax and LOST.

holidays2026.name: Iowa Sales Tax Holiday
holidays2026.items: articles of clothing and footwear with a selling price under $100 each; both state sales tax and local option tax are waived

sales.holidayNote: Held every year on the first Friday and Saturday of August (Iowa Code 423.3(68)); 2026 dates derived from that rule.

useTax.note: 6% use tax on taxable purchases when the seller did not collect Iowa sales tax; no local option use tax.

facts.text: Cars and trucks are not subject to Iowa sales tax: buyers pay a one-time fee for new registration of $10 plus 5% of the price instead.
Local option sales tax is a flat 1% approved by voters; it can be repealed only by another vote and not before it has been in effect for one year.
Where a local option tax is in force, a 1% local excise tax also applies to residential gas and electricity, which are exempt from state sales tax.
Iowa's clothing holiday is every first Friday and Saturday of August: no state or local tax on clothing and shoes priced under $100 per item.
Hotel stays carry a 5% state hotel and motel tax rather than the 6% sales tax, plus up to 7% local hotel tax.
Ibuprofen filled and labeled by a pharmacist on a prescription is exempt, but the same pill bought over the counter is taxable.

property.levied: local only: more than 2,000 levying authorities (counties, cities, school districts, etc.); the local assessor values property, the county auditor sets levy rates and the county treasurer collects; the Department of Revenue equalizes values and assesses utilities and railroads

assessment.text: Residential, commercial and industrial property is assessed at market value (farmland at a statewide productivity value) and reassessed every odd-numbered year. The county auditor then applies an 'assessment limitation' (rollback) that holds statewide growth in residential and agricultural taxable value to 3% a year; for assessment year 2025 the residential limitation was 44.5345% of assessed value.

homestead.name: Homestead Tax Exemption (SF 2472, 2026)
homestead.text: From assessment year 2026 (taxes paid September 2027 and March 2028), SF 2472 replaces the homestead credit (tax on the first $4,850 of value) with an exemption of 10% of the homestead's taxable value, at least $5,500 and at most $20,000 of taxable value; the maximum is indexed to inflation from 2027. Owners 65 or older get an additional $6,500 exemption.
homestead.applyBy: Claim with the local assessor; owners who had the credit or exemption before July 1, 2026 receive the new exemption automatically.

otherRelief.name: Homestead exemption for claimants 65 or older
otherRelief.text: Additional $6,500 of taxable value exempt; once allowed, it continues without refiling.

otherRelief.name: Disabled Veteran Homestead Property Tax Credit
otherRelief.text: Credit equal to the entire tax on the homestead for qualifying disabled veterans, surviving spouses or children; for applications from July 1, 2026 the homestead is limited to one-half acre.

otherRelief.name: Property Tax Credit (elderly and disabled)
otherRelief.text: Income-based credit; claimants 70+ qualify with household income under 250% of the federal poverty level. File with the county treasurer between January 1 and June 1, every year.

dueDates.text: First half due September 30, second half due March 31, for taxes based on the assessment of January 1 of the previous year (an 18-month cycle).

facts.text: In 2026 Iowa switched from a homestead credit to a homestead exemption worth 10% of taxable value ($5,500 minimum, $20,000 maximum), starting with taxes paid in September 2027.
Iowa homes are taxed on only part of their value: for assessment year 2025 the residential rollback was 44.5345%, so a $300,000 home had a taxable value of $133,603.
The property tax cycle takes 18 months: the January 2023 assessment produced bills due in fall 2024 and spring 2025.
The rollback limits growth of total statewide residential taxable value to 3% a year; it does not cap an individual home's assessment.
Taxpayers can request an informal review from the assessor from April 2 to 25 and protest to the local board of review from April 2 to 30.
Commercial and industrial property gets the residential rollback on its first $150,000 of value and 90% above that.

uncertain: effectiveSince of the 6% rate not on the pages read (the hotel note implies the general rate rose to 6% on July 1, 2008, but this is not stated directly); left null.
Homestead amount left null because the new exemption is a percentage (10% of taxable value, $5,500-$20,000) rather than a fixed sum; amountType kept as value-exemption.
Assessment limitation percentage for assessment year 2026 is certified by November 1, 2026 and was not yet published; 44.5345% is the 2025 figure.
2026 holiday dates (August 7-8) computed from the statutory rule (first Friday and Saturday of August) on the IDR page; IDR does not print the 2026 dates.
